Tihar is a vibrant, five-day Hindu festival of lights, flowers, and animals celebrated in Nepal and by the global Nepalese diaspora during the autumn months of October or November. Also known as Deepawali or Yama Panchak, the celebration honors various deities—such as Yama (the god of death) and Lakshmi (the goddess of wealth)—as well as nature and animals that hold sacred or practical significance. Five Days of Tihar • Day 1 (Kaag Tihar): Crows are worshipped and fed as messengers of the god of death. • Day 2 (Kukur Tihar): Dogs are adorned with garlands and honored for their loyalty and role as guardians of the afterlife. • Day 3 (Gai Tihar / Laxmi Puja): Cows are revered as symbols of wealth, and homes are illuminated with oil lamps and candles to welcome Goddess Lakshmi. #fyp #nepali #tihar #bhailo #nepalifestival
